messages:
incident-bot: EVERYONE: Pager - sudden spike in 5xx and timeouts from gateway-prod (us-east-1). Alert: gateway.error_rate > 5% for 5min. Link: https://pager.redwood.internal/incident/1781234567 :rotating_light:
Priya R: on it. joining call now. starting triage in #sre-war-room.
Alex P: saw the alert, pulling logs. grep for upstream 502/503 in last 10m.
Emily (oncall): I'm running a quick `curl` check to the /v1/generate endpoint across regions.
Samir K: I can increase gateway pool capacity if we think it's saturation. what's the current p95 latency?
Alex P: p95 jumped from 120ms -> 450ms starting ~1781234100. error rate roughly 7.2% across frontends.
Priya R: any recent deploys to gateway-prod? deploy-bot shows no deploys in the last 2 hours.
Michael S: no infra deploys. I see a spike of 502s with `upstream reset` from the model-backend cluster (mb-prod-1).
Alex P: sample logs:
```
2026-10-12T02:22:31Z gateway-prod-7d: upstream reset while reading response headers from upstream, client: 10.2.34.5, server: 10.20.1.4
2026-10-12T02:22:33Z gateway-prod-2a: upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream
```
Priya R: ok looks like backend timeouts and some connection resets. can we rule out network flaps?
Samir K: VPC metrics look flat. No packet loss. Latency to backend nodes shows occasional 3-4s spikes. Could be overloaded model-serving worker threads.
Emily (oncall): I'm toggling request-fanout to 1 for a subset of traffic to reduce backend pressure on canary route /internal/canary. Putting rule in ingress: `X-Route-Variant=single` for 5% of traffic.
Alex P: good. also enabling graceful failover to model-backend-2 cluster (mb-prod-2) for non-latency-sensitive routes. updating routing policy now.
CS-alert-bot: Notifying affected customers: A subset of API requests may return 5xx or timeouts. We are investigating.
Priya R: mitigation plan: 1) reduce concurrency by dropping heavy batch requests at gateway 2) route read-only workloads to mb-prod-2 3) temporarily increase pool size for model-backend. execute in that order.
Samir K: increasing model-backend pool by 25% on mb-prod-1 now (scaled workers +3). watch cpu and queue depth.
Michael S: applying rate limit on /v1/embeddings for non-prem teams: `quota: 10rps` via runtime-ratelimiter.
Alex P: adding KV prefix caching for repeated prompts for top callers (quick patch to gateway config). Will roll in one region first.
Emily (oncall): after routing change, error rate dropped from 7.2% -> 3.1% in 2m. p95 back to ~210ms.
Priya R: good. keep an eye for regressions. can we find root cause? logs indicate sudden surge of long-tail requests hitting legacy model variant causing thread pool exhaustion.
Alex P: correlating traffic: a large customer was running a heavy batch scoring job starting at 02:18. Their user-agent `bulk-scorer/1.2` shows a lot of long-lived connections.
CS-alert-bot: Customer UX: email to the customer success team queued. Likely high impact for that account for 4-6 minutes.
Samir K: next step: add an outbound circuit-breaker so one customer can't exhaust model-backend. I'll open a PR to add per-customer concurrency caps in the router.
Michael S: short hotfix: deploy a middleware that rejects requests with `X-Bulk-Job: true` over threshold with 429, frees up backend. Rolling patch to gateway-prod-2.
Priya R: approve hotfix. prioritize 429 over 503 so clients can backoff. Michael, coordinate with Alex for rollout.
Alex P: hotfix deployed to prod-2 and prod-3 as canary (10% traffic). 
Priya R: results?
Emily (oncall): after hotfix rollouts, error rate now 1.0% and latency stable. customer bulk job still running but rate-limited.
Priya R: escalating to SEV-2 but keeping incident channel. We need a short postmortem, runbook updates, and alert tuning so this doesn't bite us again.
Alex P: recording timeline for PM:
- 02:18 UTC: large bulk scoring job begins (bulk-scorer/1.2)
- 02:22 UTC: gateway p95 and error rate spike detected by alerts
- 02:24 UTC: routing to mb-prod-2 for canary routes enabled
- 02:25 UTC: model-backend worker pool scaled +25%
- 02:27 UTC: rate limits applied to /v1/embeddings for non-prem
- 02:29 UTC: middleware hotfix rolled to reject heavy bulk jobs -> error rate falls to ~1%
Priya R: action items (assigning):
- Priya R -> draft incident summary and customer impact (timeline + list of affected accounts) by EOD
- Samir K -> PR for per-customer concurrency caps (owner: Samir) due tomorrow 11:00 UTC
- Alex P -> add KV caching config to runbook and push gateway config (owner: Alex) due tomorrow 17:00 UTC
- Michael S -> formalize 429 hotfix as a short-lived mitigation pattern in runbook (owner: Michael) due tomorrow 09:00 UTC
- Emily (oncall) -> add automated detection for long-lived `bulk-scorer/*` UA patterns to alerts (owner: Emily) due in 48h
- CS team (not in channel) -> outreach to affected customers; CC Priya on communications
Michael S: I'll also open an alert tuning PR to raise the sensitivity threshold for transient spikes and add a 1m auto-snooze if we've already triggered an automated rollback or routing fallback.
Samir K: follow-up: we should consider a k8s-level backpressure mechanism on model workers (reduce keepalive, limit in-flight streams). I'll add to design backlog.
Priya R: customer impact summary for CS: ~6 minutes of elevated 5xx for a subset of high-volume customers. Estimated ~0.4% of overall requests failed, but 2-3 enterprise customers experienced degraded UX for 4-6 minutes.
CS-alert-bot: Draft message for customers ready, Priya to review.
Alex P: postmortem notes: root cause = unbounded bulk scoring client + no per-customer concurrency caps + legacy model variant with lower thread pool size. Mitigations worked: routing failover, worker scaling, middleware 429.
Emily (oncall): adding runbook checklist items now:
- Quick mitigation ladder: route failover -> scale workers -> apply 429 middleware -> apply per-customer cap PR
- Add observability: UA pattern detection, request duration histogram per-customer, queue-depth alert
Priya R: closing notes: great runbooked response. we'll convert this into a short ops playbook and schedule a 30min blameless debrief tomorrow 09:30 UTC. If anyone has follow-ups outside assigned tasks, drop in #oncall-postmortems. :thumbsup:
Alex P: thanks all.
incident-bot: Incident 1781234567 set to MONITORING. If conditions re-escalate, pager will fire again.
